Sets one of the 6 clip planes of a camera. While the plane is on, the camera cuts away everything that lies behind it: every point where `a*x + b*y + c*z + d` is below 0. The plane is in the world, so it stays where it is when the camera moves. A new plane is off; turn it on with [SetCameraClipPlaneEnabled](SetCameraClipPlaneEnabled). This is a BlitzLLVM extension.

`a`, `b` and `c` are the normal of the plane, which points to the side that is kept, and `d` moves the plane: a plane through the point `p` with the normal `n` has `d = -(n.x*p.x + n.y*p.y + n.z*p.z)`. The normal does not have to be one long.

Clip planes cut the triangles of the world for this camera only. They are meant for things like a water surface or a mirror, where the picture must not show what is below or behind it. Picking, culling and collisions do not use them.
@param camera  Camera handle.
@param index  Which plane, from 0 to 5.
@param a  The X of the normal.
@param b  The Y of the normal.
@param c  The Z of the normal.
@param d  How far the plane is moved along the normal.

```blitzbasic
Graphics3D 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
camera = CreateCamera()
sphere = CreateSphere(16)
PositionEntity sphere, 0, 0, 5
; Keep only what is above Y = 0: the lower half of the sphere goes away.
SetCameraClipPlane camera, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0
SetCameraClipPlaneEnabled camera, 0, True
RenderWorld
Flip
```
